transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I’m a healthcare social worker, and lately I’ve been having a really hard time concentrating and making decisions at work, even on tasks that used to feel straightforward. I finally decided to seek help because I've started making uncharacteristic errors in my case analyses and am really struggling to focus during my sessions.
Have you experienced these periods of low mood, difficulty concentrating, and lack of energy before in your life, or is this the first time you have ever felt this way?
This is actually the first time I have ever felt this way. In the past, I've always been able to handle my work and personal life without this kind of difficulty, so this is completely new to me.
Did these symptoms begin specifically following a major, identifiable change or stressful event in your life, such as a loss or a significant conflict?

Yes, this all started about a year and a half ago when my youngest child left for college, and my hospital department underwent a major restructuring. I was shifted from direct patient contact to an administrative, telehealth-heavy role, which really disrupted my sense of purpose. The combination of a quiet home and staring at spreadsheets all day has left me feeling incredibly isolated.

Since these symptoms began around the time of those life changes a year and a half ago, would you say your distress has remained relatively consistent, or have you experienced periods where your mood and energy levels dropped significantly regardless of those external circumstances?

It has been a very steady, gradual build-up since those changes happened a year and a half ago. I haven't really had sudden drops or distinct episodes; it has just been a consistent, heavy weight that hasn't lifted since everything shifted.

Since your symptoms have persisted for 18 months, have you experienced any periods where your mood felt normal for more than two months at a time, or has the distress been present almost every day throughout this entire period?
I'm not entirely sure, but it feels like this cloud has been there pretty much constantly. I don't think I've had any real periods of feeling like my old self since this all started.
Looking back over these past 18 months, have there been any stretches of two months or longer where you felt your mood was consistently back to your normal, baseline self?

No, there definitely haven't been any breaks like that. Since this started about a year and a half ago, it has just been a continuous, gradual decline without any real relief. I haven't had even a single month, let alone two, where I felt back to my normal self.
Beyond your difficulty concentrating, have you experienced other physical symptoms like changes in your sleep, appetite, or overall fatigue during these past 18 months?

Yes, I've been struggling with all of those physical changes. I usually wake up around three or four in the morning with my mind spinning, and my appetite has dropped so much that my clothes are noticeably looser. By the end of the day, I'm so exhausted that even basic tasks like loading the dishwasher feel completely overwhelming.

During these past 18 months, have you experienced any periods of psychomotor retardation or agitation so severe that others around you, such as family or colleagues, have clearly noticed and commented on your slowed-down movements or extreme restlessness?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that myself, and no one has commented on me moving noticeably slower or being physically restless. It feels more like an internal exhaustion rather than something visible in how I physically move.
